datasets.info: Qualified-income tax threshold: where the 15% rate starts. The bracket limit applies to total taxable income and qualified income sits on top of the taxable ordinary income (Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet), so this line is the limit minus that year's taxable ordinary income — it moves with the ordinary income. Qualified dividends and long-term gains stacked above it are taxed at 15%.

Qualified-income tax threshold: where the 20% rate starts. The bracket limit applies to total taxable income and qualified income sits on top of the taxable ordinary income (Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet), so this line is the limit minus that year's taxable ordinary income — it moves with the ordinary income. Qualified dividends and long-term gains stacked above it are taxed at 20%.

Qualified income before the deduction: the gap between the stack and this red line is the part of the deduction left over after ordinary income (e.g. itemized LTC costs), which shelters qualified income (LTCG first).

datasets.info: Qualified-income tax threshold: where the 15% rate starts. The bracket limit applies to total taxable income and qualified income sits on top of the taxable ordinary income (Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet), so this line is the limit minus that year's taxable ordinary income — it moves with the ordinary income. Qualified dividends and long-term gains stacked above it are taxed at 15%.

Qualified-income tax threshold: where the 20% rate starts. The bracket limit applies to total taxable income and qualified income sits on top of the taxable ordinary income (Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet), so this line is the limit minus that year's taxable ordinary income — it moves with the ordinary income. Qualified dividends and long-term gains stacked above it are taxed at 20%.

Qualified income before the deduction: the gap between the stack and this red line is the part of the deduction left over after ordinary income (e.g. itemized LTC costs), which shelters qualified income (LTCG first).
datasets.label: Deduction

datasets.info: The inflation rate the scenario assumes every year (the Inflation slider). Prices, tax thresholds that are indexed, and "today's $" amounts all follow it.

datasets.info: Nominal yearly return of this asset in the years it is in the scenario: (1 + the growth rate the projection used) × (1 + that year's inflation) − 1, i.e. the rate you enter on its card ("inflation + 4%" shows as 7% at 3% inflation). In the scenario it is flat; in a Monte Carlo trial it follows that trial's market shocks (equity-like assets share one market, real estate has its own) and its inflation.
